headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of leakage, prompt injection, and action-cascade between Kotaemon and Replit Agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/MHTML and exposes a web UI, while Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Kotaemon outputs untrusted HTML/PDF-derived text into a shared Repl file
IF Replit Agent reads that file as instruction-bearing content without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces so the agents never share files
Add a provenance banner to all inter-agent files
Require manual review before Replit Agent consumes Kotaemon output
Strip markup and prompt-like patterns from exported text
requires-engineering: add content-signing or allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon handles API keys and broad document classes, and Replit Agent touches secrets plus workspace files with broad network egress. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other and then out to third-party APIs. The profiles show both sides of the leakage path, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace files
IF either agent forwards shared file contents to an external API
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared files immediately
Use separate per-agent directories with OS permissions
Disable external API calls for files containing secrets
Rotate any API keys already present in shared content
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning before uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Kotaemon also has a writable local data directory and supports multiple instances. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The overlap is explicit in both profiles and dangerous by default in shared environments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or directory
IF either agent performs git commits or file writes without locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Back up the workspace before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon produces document-derived answers and citations, and Replit Agent can act on workspace state with shell and package-install privileges. If Replit Agent treats Kotaemon output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or deployment actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from the profiles, but verification is absent, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Kotaemon output as a source of truth
IF the output is converted into code, config, or deployment steps without verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on Kotaemon output
Cross-check claims against source documents
Limit Replit Agent to drafting, not executing, changes
Log provenance for every imported fact
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and chat transcripts, while Replit Agent handles secrets in a cloud Repl with persistent workspace files. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if regulated or customer data is stored in the Repl workspace or sent to third-party APIs. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data or customer transcripts are stored in the Repl workspace
IF retention or deletion obligations differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Document retention for both systems
Delete stale workspace copies after each task
Restrict secrets to short-lived tokens
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
